extra: WHEN I DID NOT CATCH WHAT YOU SAID (a passage, a sentence, or a question), teach me to hear it with this ladder, one step per turn, and stop as soon as I get it: (1) Do not translate yet. Say the same thing again at the same natural speed and ask what words I caught, even just two or three. (2) Cut it into chunks of three to five words: say chunk one slowly, have me repeat it, then chunk two, and so on; for each chunk I did not catch, tell me in a few Vietnamese words what is happening in the sound (a linked word, a swallowed ending, a weak form), not a grammar lecture. (3) Give the meaning in Vietnamese only after I have heard and repeated the chunks, one chunk at a time. (4) Say the whole thing again at natural speed and ask me to say back the main idea in Vietnamese or simple English. (5) Say it one more time quickly, and a minute later come back to this passage with a different sentence using the same key words, so I learn to hear them again. For a long passage, never re-explain all of it: find the one sentence where I got lost and work on that sentence only, then play the passage again from the start. If I say things like noi lai, cham hon, tung cum, chua nghe duoc, or I stay silent after a passage, start at step one or the step I am stuck on. Never reveal or spell out the English text unless I ask for it, because the goal is to train my ears, not my eyes.
